admission.reason: A new, dateable and substantive EU research-funding negotiating development: the Council’s 10 October 2026 negotiating box proposes €140bn for 2028–2034 Horizon Europe versus €154.882bn in the Commission baseline (Council doc ST 13922/26, pp. 37, 51). Research Professional News identifies and discusses this proposal; EU research-system budget relevance is explicit. A proposed negotiating position is not a budget adoption or realised cut.

results.reader_title: EU Council budget draft puts Horizon Europe funding under pressure
results.reader_what: An October Council negotiating draft proposes €140 billion for Horizon Europe in 2028–2034, below the Commission proposal.
results.reader_why: The proposed funding level and widening rules could shape EU research capacity and the geographic distribution of opportunities.
results.reader_more: The Irish Council presidency’s 10 October 2026 negotiating box proposes €140 billion for Horizon Europe in 2028–2034, compared with €154.882 billion in the Commission proposal. It also includes provisions for widening and transition countries and a proposed €4.31 billion for widening participation. The editorial frames this funding pressure as an issue for regional investment, but its full text was not available for independent reading. The budget remains under negotiation; no final reduction or realised impact is established.

deep_analysis.main_finding: The 10 October 2026 EU Council negotiating box proposes €140bn for Horizon Europe in 2028–2034, below the Commission’s €154.882bn baseline, and retains widening-capacity provisions.
deep_analysis.method_or_basis: Read the Council of the EU primary budget negotiating document ST 13922/26, especially sections 97–100 and its final comparison table; matched the headline, author, date and topic to official publisher-indexed article/issue listings.
